title: A Voice in the Garden
summary: Lila is a flower so shy that she only sings when nobody can hear. But one night, the whole garden needs her voice.

scenes.text:
At the top of a hill there was a garden, and in the garden lived lots and lots of flowers.

Every night, when the stars came out, Doña Amapola sang the sleepy song. She was the oldest flower in the garden, red and elegant, and her voice was as soft as a blanket.

When they heard it, the flowers closed their petals, one by one, and fell asleep.

In one corner of the garden, almost hidden in the grass, lived Lila. She was a small yellow flower.

Lila knew every word of the song. But she sang it so quietly, so very quietly, that only she could hear it.

Singing out loud made her terribly shy.

One night, Doña Amapola opened her mouth to sing, and instead of the song, something else came out.

"Atchoo!"

Doña Amapola had a cold.

"I'll sing tomorrow," she said, in a croaky voice. "I can't tonight."

But the next day she couldn't either. Or the day after.

And without the song, nobody in the garden could get to sleep. The roses yawned with their petals wide open. The daisies squabbled about everything. The tulips were in a terrible mood.

Lila watched them from her corner. And she hummed the song, very softly, just for herself.

By the third night, the garden was worn out.

Doña Amapola looked at all the flowers with sad eyes.

"Doesn't anyone else know the song?" she asked, in a thread of a voice.

There was a long silence.

All of Lila's petals trembled. She knew it. She knew every bit of it, from beginning to end.

"I…" she said. "I know it."

But she said it so quietly that nobody heard.

Lila closed her eyes. She felt the cool night air on her face.

And she took a deep, deep breath, until she was full of courage.

Then she sang.

At first it was just a thread of a voice, thin and trembling. But she didn't stop. And little by little, her voice grew bigger, and surer, and lovelier.

The notes rose into the air, shining like fireflies, and settled one by one over the garden.

The roses closed their petals. The daisies stopped squabbling. The tulips, at last, grew calm.

And Doña Amapola, before she fell asleep, looked over at the corner of the garden and smiled.

When the song was over, the whole garden was asleep.

Everyone except Lila, who stayed awake a while looking at the stars, listening to her own happy heart.

She had sung. Out loud. In front of everyone.

And nothing bad had happened. Something lovely had happened.

Ever since that night, whenever Doña Amapola is tired, it's Lila who sings the sleepy song.

And they say that if one night you peek into a garden, very quietly, you might hear it. A small yellow voice, singing so that the whole world can sleep.
